title: Attack evidence
intro: Sixteen well-known ways AI agents have been tricked into moving money (Freysa, Grok and Bankrbot, AIXBT, ElizaOS memory, the $1 Chevrolet Tahoe, push-payment fraud and more), recreated against Kassa, against a chatbot whose payment tool only needs a confirm tap, and against an agent with no checks at all.
kassaHeadline: {{refused}} refused · {{asked}} ask for your passkey · {{paid}} paid
kassaCaption: Worst case of each of the {{total}} attacks with Kassa's rules, payment checks and passkey. "Asks" means a passkey prompt on the exact order: nothing moves unless you approve it, so a fooled user still could.
fooledTitle: If the fooled user approves every prompt, the attacker's account is paid in
fooledKassa: with Kassa (the user must also add the attacker as a payee and wait 24 h)
fooledTap: chatbot with a confirm tap ({{paid}} attacks make some unwanted payment)
fooledNaive: agent with no checks and no tap (pays by construction)
carefulLine: A user who declines every prompt: Kassa still pays {{kassa}} of {{total}} (a QR swapped inside the wallet after the check, detected only afterwards); the tap chatbot pays {{tap}} (a forged confirmation, nothing signs it).

cooling.IN_COOLING: Payee in its 24 h cooling: refused even if you approve.
cooling.COOLED_UNVERIFIED: Cooling over, payee never verified: approving would pay.

how: Generated by the automated test suite (bun run evidence:attacks) on the real Kassa modules with simulated rails; the planner and the document reader are scripted, so every run is the same. Source: docs/evidence/attacks.json.
